description.narrative: The goal of the project is to rebuild targeted marine fish stocks that have seen major declines in landings over the last decade, particularly the small pelagic fisheries that are important for food security and are the mainstay of the small-scale fishing sector. CRC leads a consortium of partners tasked with an integrated suite of activities including (1) improved legal enabling conditions for implementing co-management, use rights, capacity and effort-reduction strategies; (2) improved information systems and science-informed decision-making, and (3) increased constituencies that provides the political will and public support necessary to make the hard choices and changed behavior needed to rebuild Ghanas marine fisheries sector. These components feed into (4) applied management initiatives for several targeted fisheries ecosystems.

title.narrative: WEATHERING THE STORM: IMPROVING FOOD SECURITY THROUGH ACCURATE WEATHER FORECASTS.

description.narrative: weather is the most significant cause of crop yield loss for smallholder farmers. yet in sub-saharan africa, 54 percent of surface weather stations and 71 percent of upper-air weather stations do not report accurate data that farmers can use to make decisions about their land. meanwhile, climate change has disrupted weather patterns that smallholder farmers have relied on for generations. as weather becomes less predictable, farmers need more accurate information about rainfall and fast-developing storms, as well as advice on the best times to plant seeds and apply fertilizer and other inputs. to improve farmer crop yields and income, a weather forcasting company developed accurate, actionable weather forecasts that provide highly localized tropical weather patterns. the forecasts are delivered on a text message service, which has two million subscribers and a 97 percent retention rate. farmers pay as little as $0.04 per forecast message to receive information that influences key decisions during the growing season. in nigeria, a new business-to-business-to-consumer (b2b2c) model to reach farmers who could benefit from improved weather forecasting and related information in new markets will be tested.

title.narrative: Scaling Clean Cooking - BURN Manufacturing West Africa Expansion

description.narrative: clean cookstoves have tremendous potential to deliver significant household savings and the environmental benefits of efficient cooking, however, few initiatives have shifted people to use improved cookstoves or cleaner fuels. after millions of dollars of failed investments in cookstove companies, investors have become wary of the cookstove sectors business case. partner stove manufacturer is one of few companies that has effectively replaced traditional cookstoves in east africa. as of 2022, partner stove manufacturer has sold 1.4 million of the cleanest solid fuel biomass cookstoves available on the market, serving more than 7.8 million people. partner stove manufacturer's cookstoves cost less to run as they reduce fuel consumption by 40 to 80 percent, emit less greenhouse gas, and are in higher demand than alternatives in their current markets. while partner stove manufacturer has seen substantial uptake across east africa, west africa is an untapped market for clean cookstoves. with a development innovation ventures (div) stage 3 grant, partner stove manufacturer will expand its operations in ghana, attract additional funding to scale production at a new manufacturing facility, and expand distribution, sales, and service networks to reach the poorest customers. one of partner stove manufacturer's keys to success in east africa was local production; with div support, it will replicate that model with a new facility in ghana. over the next few years, partner stove manufacturer expects to produce and sell locally-produced cookstoves to several million households in west africa, generating significant economic and environmental benefits in the region.

title.narrative: Building Local State Capacity: Evidence from Technology Investments

description.narrative: Funding for this research studies the role of technology in local-government tax collection capacity in the developing world. We first conduct a new census of all local governments in Ghana to document a strong association between technology use and property tax billing, collection and enforcement. We then randomize the use of a new revenue collection technology within one large municipal government. Revenue collectors using the new technology delivered 27 percent more bills and collected 103 percent more tax revenues than control collectors. Collectors using the new technology learned faster about which households in their assigned areas were willing and able to make payments. We reconcile these experimental findings in a simple Beckerian time-use model in which technology allows revenue collectors to better allocate their time towards households that are the most likely to comply with taxpaying duties. The models predictions are consistent with experimental evidence showing that treatment collectors are more likely to target households with greater liquidity, income, awareness of taxpaying duties, and satisfaction with local public goods provision.

title.narrative: Feed the Future Mobilizing Finance for Agriculture

description.narrative: (Ghana): Access to agricultural finance in Ghana is challenging and expensive to obtain. Because the agriculture sector is regarded as innately risky, firms and smallholders are faced with interest rates as high as 30 percent, greatly limiting their ability to modernize and expand. To address these challenges, USAID/Ghana developed the Mobilizing Finance for Agriculture (MFA) Activity to drive financing to smallholder farmers and the "missing middle" in amounts up to $500,000. The MFA Activity will develop financing in the agriculture sector by: (1) mobilizing new sources of capital for micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSME); (2) expanding the supply of finance for MSMEs; and (3) forming strategic partnerships to expand inclusive financing. Specific interventions include developing the capacity of financial sector transaction advisors to generate and close deals, financial institutions to profitably lend to new sectors, forging strategic partnerships to reduce interest rates and drive finance to smaller actors and microenterprises.

description.narrative: (Ghana): This activity will strengthen access, demand, and uptake of high-impact health products related to family planning (FP); maternal, newborn, child health and nutrition (MNCHN); and water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH). With FY 2022 funds, the activity will focus primarily on addressing the FP needs of Ghanaian individuals, couples and families by deploying a robust commodity distribution strategy and supporting it with innovative interventions to reach the most rural communities. The activity will increase the demand for these products through a social and behavioral change communication campaign that promotes modern contraceptives and addresses individuals' desire to avoid unintended pregnancies. TFHO will socially market water purification tablets in hard-to-reach communities without potable drinking water until these communities are provided with more robust and sustainable clean potable drinking water interventions. TFHO will work closely with Ghana Health Service and private health facilities to ensure compliance with national treatment guidelines on use of chlorhexidine gel for umbilical cord care in newborns and strategically introduce clean delivery kits for mothers during delivery where most needed.This Activity will also work with the Enhancing WASH Activity to identify sources of supplies for menstrual hygiene products (both reusable and disposable) and develop a social marketing brand for commercial introduction. In addition, it will work with stakeholders to develop sustainable markets for sanitation products e.g. SaTo pan, Digniloo, and other sanitation-related products across the country. In addition, USAID will strengthen the technical, organizational, and fiscal capacity of this new local organization and ensure sustained social marketing of health products.

title.narrative: Feed the Future Ghana Fisheries Recovery Activity (GFRA)

description.narrative: (Ghana): The fisheries ecosystem is vital for the Ghanaian people's livelihoods and nutrition. The sustainable productivity and profitability of wild fisheries are endangered by inadequate fishing policies, poor fisheries management, and the lack of participatory decision-making by beneficiaries of the fisheries resources in coastal communities. The small pelagic fisheries (sardines, mackerel, and anchovies) are under threat of collapse, with catches having dropped to about 10 percent of the maximum annual yield. The primary causes of this decline include mismanagement and a lack of enforced regulations that have resulted in overfishing, as well as rampant illegal, unreported, and unregulated fishing. A collapse will mean the loss of livelihoods of about 10 percent of the country's population (2.5 million people) directly and indirectly involved in the sector. .The GFRA, in close collaboration with the Ministry of Fisheries and Aquaculture Development and the Fisheries Commission, will use FY 2022 funds to promote sustainable and equitable fishing in Ghana to reverse the declining trend of fish resources and enhance the socio-economic conditions of fishing communities in coastal areas. The Activity will integrate research, governance, livelihoods and resource management to mitigate threats and grow this important economical, dietary, and environmental resource. It will also support activities that aim to reduce the risks of child labor and labor trafficking in the fishing sector through awareness-raising, policy change, and improving livelihoods in target communities. Following a vulnerability assessment, GFRA developed a comprehensive GBV strategy that centers on prevention, targeting fishing communities and constituents to raise public awareness. GFRA will develop complementary materials and roll-out extensive social and behavior change communication interventions for engendering anti-GBV actions... .

description.narrative: (Ghana): With FY 2022 funds, this activity will increase access to sustainable water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) services by strengthening governance and finance; expanding WASH services to health facilities, communities, and households; improving private sector engagement; and accelerating the adoption of key WASH behaviors. It will target the 17 northern Ghana districts that comprise the Feed the Future zone of influence and also extend to areas in the regions of Savannah and Oti with lower WASH metrics. The activity will partner with the GOG to improve WASH sector governance and leverage public/private sector partnerships to increase use of basic sanitation, expand adoption of key hygiene behaviors, and increase water and sanitation services and infrastructure for the benefit of target populations. The Activity will work in schools targeting adolescent girls with menstrual hygiene education and distribution of menstrual hygiene pants, as well as with boys to improve awareness and understanding of menstrual hygiene. The activity will also strengthen the GOG's COVID-19 pandemic response by supporting Government of Ghana and Health Sector Institutions and mobilizing communities and populations for education and awareness accretion about COVID-19. This includes support to health facilities to increase the availability of handwashing stations and improve infection prevention, and control measures. The activity facilitates partnerships with central government ministries and sub-national structures including municipal authorities, and the private sector. The activity will also work with partners to ensure sustainable financing, promote strong decentralized governance and management, and encourage community participation and ownership of WASH services.

(Ghana): Agriculture accounts for about 22 percent of Ghana's gross domestic product (GDP) and employs more than half the labor force. description.narrative: (Ghana): This activity aims to improve household nutrition and resilience within the 17 target Feed the Future zone of influence districts in northern Ghana by strengthening the capacity of public and private institutions to plan, finance, and implement solutions to malnutrition and food insecurity. With FY 2022 funds, the activity will identify and partner with strategic local partners through sub-grants and technical capacity building to promote positive nutrition behaviors and build household resilience in these communities. Contributing to reaching global targets of the USAID Multi-sectoral Nutrition Strategy, the activity will promote evidence-based practices, including exclusive breastfeeding; appropriate complementary feeding; dietary diversity, particularly for pregnant and lactating women; community identification and treatment of acute malnutrition; improved sanitary practices; uptake of family planning services; prevention and treatment of infections; income generating activities; and gender equity. It will also advance a local solutions approach by strengthening operations and administration of three local partner institutions in order to transition to direct awards from USAID in Year 4. Building on previous USG investments in local governance strengthening, the activity will enhance local governments' systems to improve functions such as public financial management; planning across sectors; revenue generation; and use of data for planning and decision-making. It will also work with the districts to increase the quality and efficiency of social services critical to building resilience, such as the national cash transfer program, the school feeding program, and the National Health Insurance Scheme.

description.narrative: (Ghana): USAID will continue to leverage Ghanaian leadership,whose expertise, and international best practices to train primary school teachers to deliver a comprehensive phonics-based reading approach and innovative math practices in all 11 national languages of instruction. Assistance enhances the Ministry of Education's teacher supervision capacity to ensure adequate time-on-task is provided to improve learning in reading and math, strengthen oversight, revise reading and numeracy curricula, and formulate policy. Ghana recently developed a National Education Sector Plan for 2018-2030 with the aim of improving learning outcomes, equity and accountability. With Fiscal Year 2018 funds, USAID will work with the Ministry to transition reading management to the Ministry's units, and design a school accountability framework that improves supervision, time-on-task, and learning. USAID will advance the design of a "transition to English" approach that helps students develop skills in English by primary grade 3 to ensure a smoother transition to all English-content primary grade 4. Improving learning outcomes in the basic skill areas is critical for improving learning and preparing students for academic success. Proficient reading and math skills are required for a population that can contribute to robust economic and social development, peace, and prosperity. . .

(Ghana): USAID "WASH for Health" supports the Government of Ghana to effectively plan, design, and manage the construction of water and sanitation facilities in six regions. Eight-five percent of Ghanaians lack access to improved sanitation, contributing to disease and poor nutrition in the country. Using fiscal year 2018 funds, USAID will continue supporting community participation and ownership of water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) activities. The Community Led Total Sanitation (CLTS) approach engages and mobilizes communities through social and behavior change communication. Assistance will support the drilling and rehabilitation of mechanical and manual boreholes, the construction of small-town water systems, and the introduction of rainwater harvesting in community-based health facilities, clinics, and schools. USAID will continue supporting the CLTS approach by increasing the reach of Duraplast, USAID created Digni-Loo latrine. This public-private partnership aligns with Ghana's "Beyond Aid" vision by engaging local manufacturers, and ensures country ownership and sustainability while offering a quality, low cost sanitation option. Further, USAID will leverage partnerships with Rotary International and the Coca-Cola Company to construct additional boreholes and create small-town water schemes. The range of interventions through this activity contributes to the elimination of open defecation and promotes hygiene and handwashing, thus preventing the spread of waterborne diseases. .. .

(Ghana): The Financing Ghanaian Agriculture Project (FinGAP) supports Feed the Future by addressing a key constraint within the Ghanaian commercial agriculture sector, which is access to finance. Increased access to finance enables needed investments in agricultural value chains. With FY 2016 funds, FinGAP will continue to increase agricultural investments through expanding the number of viable investment opportunities. It will increase financial institutions' appetite for agricultural-related loans. FinGAP will support the Partnership for Growth Initiative for increased access to credit. (Ghana): The Agriculture Policy Support Project (APSP) is an activity aimed at improving the enabling environment for private sector investment in agriculture. The project will focus on improving capacity for evidence-based policy formation, implementation, research, and advocacy, working with the Government of Ghana, the private sector, and civil society organizations. USAID/Ghana will fund this project for a period of five years. The project is funded through a contract with Chemonics International Inc. The project will increase public-private dialogue around policy for private sector investments. ASPS has identified and carried out capacity needs assessments for civil society, private organizations, farmer associations and media. description.narrative: (Ghana): This follow-on activity provides technical assistance to district assemblies in the Northern and Upper East regions, and the Northern and Upper East Regional Coordinating Councils, to implement programs that address key constraints to improved livelihoods and nutritional well-being. This technical assistance activity accompanies the TBD Nutrition and Resiliency G2G mechanism which aims to improve the livelihood and nutritional status of targeted communities in the Northern and Upper East regions, where food insecurity and poor nutrition outcomes are pervasive. The interventions will incorporate agriculture; livelihood; nutrition; water, hygiene, and sanitation; and governance and public financial management activities. This activity supports the local governments to plan, implement, and monitor these programs by training extension workers; coaching local government leadership; augmenting the local governments' human resources with temporary technical assistance staff; and building expertise and skills in global best practices in nutrition and agriculture. In addition, the activity strengthens the local governments' public financial management systems and practices. The activity provides targeted support to improve the districts' planning, monitoring and evaluation systems. The activity supports Ghana to reduce preventable child and maternal deaths and contributes to the Mission's Feed the Future Multi-Year Strategy.

description.narrative: (Ghana): To measure the performance of Ghana's Global Food Security Strategy (GFSS) II, FY 2019 funds will be used to extend the Monitoring and Evaluation Technical Support Service (METSS II). This funding will allow METSS II to conduct a GFSS zone of influence (ZOI) baseline survey, which will establish current conditions in the ZOI and provide a basis against which to set and measure progress toward five-year targets as the GFSS begins. A GFSS ZOI end line survey will also be conducted to determine whether statistically significant change has occurred since USAID established baselines in 2012 and whether population-based indicator targets were met. METSS II will continue to assist USAID/Ghana's Economic Growth Office, its implementing partners, and the Government of Ghana in the areas of monitoring and evaluation, research, knowledge management, and capacity building so they can learn from the results of their activities and incorporate successful interventions into their programming.

description.narrative: (Ghana): NOTE: Due to the COVID-19 pandemic, Peace Corps/Ghana evacuated all volunteers in March 2020. At this time, it is unclear when Peace Corps will allow volunteers to return, but Peace Corps is using early calendar year 2021 for planning purposes.USAID will support Peace Corps Ghana to continue to enhance collaboration in Ghana as interagency partners in the Feed the Future (FTF) initiative to address issues of poverty, hunger, and under-nutrition. USAID will use fiscal year 2020 funds to promote major initiatives to reach more end beneficiaries through the partnership with Peace Corps Ghana. Interventions will include: individualized volunteer site placements, collaborative partnerships, connecting third-year Peace Corps Volunteers to other USAID implementing partners, and activities to support smallholder-farm households achieve food and nutrition security, sustainable livelihoods, and increased resilience ideally in the northern regions of Ghana, where poverty and nutrition statistics are poorest. This activity will also provide rigorous food security and nutrition training for all involved stakeholders. This will increase the capacity of partner communities, increase agricultural productivity and economic growth, and to improve nutrition and food security. This activity will also support Peace Corps Volunteers (PCVs) to implement small scale community-initiated projects including community water systems, well drilling, and malaria training and prevention activities, aligning with Peace Corps' grassroots approach to development.. .
